name: network_baseline_security_group_rule
description: Manages one inbound rule on a duploai_network_baseline's primary AWS security group — the network-scoped sibling of duploai_resource_group_security_group_rule. Each resource is a single rule with exactly one source: an IPv4 CIDR, an IPv6 CIDR, or a resource group whose own security group becomes the source. Declare several blocks for several rules. AWS assigns each rule an id, which is what Terraform tracks and what the API updates and deletes by.

invalidWhen.message: For tcp and udp, to_port must be greater than or equal to from_port — the rule allows the range from the lower value to the higher one. This does not apply to icmp/icmpv6, where the two fields carry the ICMP type and code (type 8, code 0 is a valid echo request), nor to -1, where ports are ignored.

from_port must not be set when ip_protocol is "-1": the rule already allows every protocol and port, so the API ignores the value and reports -1 on read — leaving a diff that no apply can settle. Remove from_port, or name a protocol (tcp/udp) if you want a port range.

to_port must not be set when ip_protocol is "-1": the rule already allows every protocol and port, so the API ignores the value and reports -1 on read — leaving a diff that no apply can settle. Remove to_port, or name a protocol (tcp/udp) if you want a port range.

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: ID of the workspace that owns the network.

attributes.name: network_id
attributes.description: ID of the duploai_network_baseline whose primary security group this rule is added to. Read it from that resource's network_id attribute. The network is workspace-scoped, so no environment or resource group is involved.

attributes.name: ip_protocol
attributes.description: IP protocol the rule allows: tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, or -1 for all protocols. from_port and to_port are required for tcp and udp; for icmp and icmpv6 they carry the ICMP type and code and default to -1 (all types, all codes) when omitted; for -1 they are ignored.

attributes.name: from_port
attributes.description: Start of the allowed port range for tcp/udp (1-65535), or the ICMP type for icmp/icmpv6 where -1 means all types. Required for tcp and udp.

attributes.name: to_port
attributes.description: End of the allowed port range for tcp/udp (1-65535), or the ICMP code for icmp/icmpv6 where -1 means all codes. Required for tcp and udp, and must be greater than or equal to from_port.

attributes.name: cidr_ipv4
attributes.description: IPv4 CIDR allowed by this rule, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 or 203.0.113.4/32. Exactly one source is required: cidr_ipv4, cidr_ipv6, or source_resource_group_id.

attributes.name: cidr_ipv6
attributes.description: IPv6 CIDR allowed by this rule, e.g. 2001:db8::/64. Exactly one source is required: cidr_ipv4, cidr_ipv6, or source_resource_group_id.

attributes.name: source_resource_group_id
attributes.description: ID of a resource group whose primary security group is the source of this rule — the platform resolves it to that group's sg- id. The referenced group must be in the same workspace as the network and must already have its security group provisioned. Exactly one source is required: cidr_ipv4, cidr_ipv6, or source_resource_group_id.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Free-text description for the rule. The platform applies it to the rule's source entry, so it appears on the rule in the AWS console.

attributes.name: security_group_rule_id
attributes.description: AWS-assigned id of this rule (sgr-...). The API updates and deletes rules by this value.

attributes.name: security_group_rule_arn
attributes.description: ARN of this security group rule.

attributes.name: group_id
attributes.description: ID of the security group the rule belongs to — the resource group's primary security group.

attributes.name: referenced_group_id
attributes.description: ID of the source security group, when the source is another security group. Populated when source_resource_group_id is set.
